birth:isaac_616@a355cb.note: Abraham was 100 when Isaac was born (21:5). The text gives no year; the BC year depends on dating outside Scripture.

birth:ishmael_630@3f7521.note: Abram was 86 when Hagar bare Ishmael (16:16). The text gives no year; the BC year depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:abraham-and-lot-separate@58b44d.note: Timing only: after the Egypt trip (13:1) and before Ishmael's birth at Abram's age 86 (16:16). The BC year depends on outside dating.

date:abraham-goes-to-egypt@c351f0.note: Abram left Haran aged 75 (12:4), then went down to Egypt in famine (12:10). Timing only; the BC year depends on outside dating.

date:abrahamic-covenant@c351f0.note: The call and promise come before Abram left Haran at 75 (12:1-4). The text gives no year; the BC year depends on outside dating.

date:birth-of-isaac@a355cb.note: Sarah bare the son 'at the set time' (21:2) when Abraham was 100 (21:5). The BC year depends on outside dating.

date:birth-of-ishmael@3f7521.note: Hagar bare Ishmael when Abram was 86 (16:16). The text gives no year; the BC year depends on outside dating.

date:lifetime-of-abraham@5bf47d.note: Lived 175 years (25:7). His age of 86 at Ishmael's birth (16:16) points to a birth near -1995, not -1996. The BC years depend on outside dating.

date:lifetime-of-isaac@88c666.note: Isaac lived 180 years (35:28), born when Abraham was 100 (21:5). 35:28 is outside this passage; the BC years depend on outside dating.

date:lifetime-of-ishmael@e46c31.note: Ishmael lived 137 years (25:17), born when Abram was 86 (16:16). 25:17 is outside this passage; the BC years depend on outside dating.

date:sodom-destroyed@ae51cc.note: The visit promises Isaac within a year (18:10, 18:14), then fire falls on Sodom (19:24). Timing fits the year before Isaac's birth; the BC year depends on outside dating.

death:ishmael_630@60d5db.note: Ishmael died aged 137 (25:17), which is outside this passage. The passage gives no year; the BC year depends on outside dating.

near:beer-lahai-roi_167>kadesh-barnea_66.note: The well is 'between Kadesh and Bered' (16:14). Taking that Kadesh as Kadesh-barnea is a reading, supported by 14:7.

near:moreh_817>shechem_1069@c9c1c8.note: Abram came 'unto the place of Sichem, unto the plain of Moreh' (12:6). Reading the two as one site, Sichem being Shechem, makes 'near' a reading.
